We need to find a test whose asymptotic power approaches 1 as *n* approaches infinity, given a significance level alpha = 0.05.\\n     6\\t\\n     7\\t**Calculating mu<sub>n</sub> and epsilon<sub>n</sub>**\\n     8\\t\\n     9\\t*   mu<sub>n</sub> = sqrt(2r log n) = sqrt(2 * 0.45 * log n) = sqrt(0.9 * log n)\\n    10\\t*   epsilon<sub>n</sub> = n<sup>-beta</sup> = n<sup>-0.85</sup>\\n    11\\t\\n    12\\t**Analyzing the Options**\\n    13\\t\\n    14\\t**A) One-sided z-test based on the sample mean,  $\\\\bar{X}$**\\n    15\\t\\n    16\\t*   The null hypothesis is *H<sub>0</sub>*: *mu<sub>i</sub> = 0* for all *i*.\\n    17\\t*   The alternative hypothesis is *H<sub>1</sub>*: *mu<sub>i</sub> > 0* for at least one *i*.\\n    18\\t*   Under *H<sub>0</sub>*, the sample mean $\\\\bar{X}$ follows a normal distribution with mean 0 and variance 1/n, so $\\\\bar{X} \\\\sim N(0, 1/n)$.\\n    19\\t*   Under *H<sub>1</sub>*, the variance of $\\\\bar{X}$ is more complex due to the different distributions of the individual *X<sub>i</sub>*.\\n    20\\t*   As *n* approaches infinity, $\\\\bar{X}$ converges to a standard normal distribution.
